objectives.knowledge: Explain clinical trial architecture (Phases I–III), why AAV5 is selected for CNS gene therapy, and the 3-stage molecular mechanism of AMT-130 (AAV5 vector architecture, MRI-guided stereotactic CED, and Dicer/RISC RNAi).
objectives.application: Analyse the M4 challenge of non-allele-specific HTT silencing (toxic gain-of-function vs wild-type HTT loss-of-function) and interpret primary clinical trial data (CSF mHTT, NfL, cUHDRS).
objectives.evaluation: Evaluate trial methodology (sham controls, N=29 cohort size, irreversible intracranial surgery) and align coursework to OCR Unit F172 NEA Task 2 Pass (P5, P7, P8), Merit (M3, M4, M5), and Distinction (D3, D4, D5) criteria.

terminology.def: An investigational AAV5-miRNA gene therapy delivering engineered microRNA (miHTT) directly into the caudate and putamen via MRI-guided stereotactic CED to silence human HTT mRNA via RNA interference.
A non-pathogenic viral vector (~4.7 kb payload limit) with high neuronal tropism that persists as a stable circular nuclear episome in post-mitotic neurons without integrating into host chromosomes.

Normal huntingtin (wtHTT) supports axonal vesicle transport, synaptic survival, and cortical BDNF transcription; because AMT-130's miHTT is non-allele-specific, it lowers both toxic mHTT and healthy wtHTT.

A sensitive CSF biomarker of active neuroaxonal damage; initial post-operative spike from catheter placement followed by a -8.2% decline below baseline at 36 months indicates slowed neurodegeneration.

OCR Unit F172 coursework criteria: Pass (P5 relevance, P7 delivery, P8 counselling), Merit (M3 therapeutic context, M4 challenges analysis, M5 counselling benefits), and Distinction (D3 viable cure discussion, D4/D5 holistic evaluation).

slides.title: Starter Retrieval Grid: Genetics & Gene Delivery Recall
slides.subtitle: Do Now Activity (5 Minutes) · Retrieve Prior Knowledge from Lessons 3–9
keyTakeaways: Card 1 (L5 Mutation): Autosomal dominant CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion (>36 repeats) in exon 1 of the HTT gene on chromosome 4.
Card 2 (L9 Viral Tropism): AAV5 displays high natural tropism for post-mitotic neurons and persists as a safe non-integrating nuclear episome.

Card 3 (L9 Delivery Routes): In vivo = systemic/local administration into body; Ex vivo = cells modified outside body and re-infused; In situ = targeted focal injection directly into diseased organ/nucleus.
Card 4 (L9 BBB Challenge): Convection-Enhanced Delivery (CED) uses a stereotactic microcannula and positive-pressure bulk flow directly into the striatum, bypassing brain capillary tight junctions.
Card 5 (L3 Central Dogma): Post-transcriptional gene silencing (translation stage)—RISC cleaves cytoplasmic mRNA transcripts before ribosome translation.
Card 6 (L6 Inheritance): 50% (1 in 2) probability of inheriting the expanded autosomal dominant allele from a heterozygous affected parent.

reveals.label: Card 1: L5 Mutation (The Huntington's Locus)
reveals.question: What trinucleotide repeat expansion on chromosome 4 causes Huntington's disease, and what is the pathological threshold?
reveals.answer: An expanded CAG (cytosine-adenine-guanine) trinucleotide repeat in exon 1 of the HTT gene on chromosome 4p16.3. Pathological threshold is ≥36 CAG repeats (≥40 repeats shows 100% full penetrance).

reveals.label: Card 2: L9 Viral Tropism (Vector Selection)
reveals.question: Why is Adeno-Associated Virus serotype 5 (AAV5) selected for adult striatal neurons instead of a lentiviral vector?
reveals.answer: Adult striatal medium spiny neurons are post-mitotic (non-dividing). AAV5 has high neuronal tropism and persists stably as a non-integrating circular episome in the nucleus, avoiding the insertional mutagenesis/oncogenesis risk of integrating lentiviruses.

reveals.label: Card 3: L9 Delivery Routes (Administration)
reveals.question: Distinguish between In Vivo, Ex Vivo, and In Situ gene therapy administration routes.
reveals.answer: Ex Vivo modifies harvested patient cells in the lab before re-infusion (e.g., Casgevy HSCs). In Vivo administers vectors directly into the body. In Situ is a focal administration directly into the target anatomical structure (e.g., intrastriatal AMT-130 infusion).

reveals.label: Card 4: L9 BBB Challenge (Surgical Bypass)
reveals.question: How does stereotactic Convection-Enhanced Delivery (CED) overcome the Blood-Brain Barrier?
reveals.answer: Brain capillary endothelial tight junctions block >98% of systemic viral vectors. Stereotactic CED places microcatheters directly through cranial burr holes into the caudate and putamen, using a positive-pressure gradient to drive homogeneous interstitial vector flow.

reveals.label: Card 5: L3 Central Dogma (Gene Silencing)
reveals.question: At which stage of gene expression (transcription vs translation) does microRNA (miRNA) gene silencing operate?
reveals.answer: Post-transcriptionally (preventing translation). Engineered miRNA binds complementarily to cytoplasmic HTT mRNA via the RISC complex, cleaving the mRNA transcript so ribosomes cannot translate toxic mHTT protein.

reveals.label: Card 6: L6 Inheritance (Genetic Risk)
reveals.question: Huntington's disease is autosomal dominant. What is the inheritance probability from a heterozygous affected parent?
reveals.answer: 50% (0.5 or 1 in 2) risk for each biological child (male or female) of inheriting the expanded HTT allele from a heterozygous (Hh) affected parent.

slides.subtitle: OCR Unit F172 NEA Task 2 | Criteria P5 & P7 (PO2)
keyTakeaways: Delivery Vehicle: Recombinant AAV5 viral capsid (adeno-associated virus serotype 5) with high affinity for striatal neurons.

slides.title: Why Adeno-Associated Viruses (AAV) for Gene Therapy?
slides.subtitle: OCR Unit F172 NEA Task 2 | Criteria P5, P7 (PO2) & M3, M4 (PO3)
keyTakeaways: High Neuronal Tropism: AAV5 capsid naturally binds receptors on non-dividing post-mitotic striatal neurons.
Episomal Safety (Non-Integrating): Persists as stable circular nuclear episomes without integrating into host chromosomes—avoiding insertional mutagenesis and oncogenesis.
Low Immunogenicity & Multi-Year Durability: Lower innate inflammatory response than adenoviral vectors; single dose drives multi-year miHTT transcription in non-dividing neurons.
Packaging Limit Fit (~4.7 kb): Although full-length HTT cDNA (~9.5 kb) exceeds AAV's ~4.7 kb ceiling, the compact engineered miHTT hairpin cassette (<1.5 kb) fits comfortably inside the AAV5 capsid.

reveals.label: Question: Why Adeno-Associated Viruses (AAV5) for AMT-130?
reveals.question: Why is Adeno-Associated Virus serotype 5 (AAV5) chosen as the viral vector for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease (P5, P7, M3, M4)?
reveals.answer:
1. Neuronal Tropism: AAV5 efficiently transduces post-mitotic striatal neurons.
2. Non-Integrating Episomal Safety: AAV5 DNA forms stable circular episomes in the nucleus without integrating into host chromosomes, preventing insertional mutagenesis/oncogenesis.
3. Durable Expression: Because adult neurons do not divide, nuclear episomes are not diluted by mitosis, enabling multi-year miHTT expression from a single dose.
4. Payload Fit (~4.7 kb): While full-length HTT cDNA (~9.5 kb) is too large for AAV's 4.7 kb limit, the compact miHTT RNAi cassette (<1.5 kb) fits easily inside AAV5.

slides.title: Video Activity: Summarise the Role of microRNA (miRNA)
slides.subtitle: Watch from 2:28 (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cK-OGB1_ELE&t=148s) · OCR NEA Task 2 Criteria P5 (PO2) & M3 (PO3)

webEmbed.title: Video Activity: Summarise the Role of microRNA (miRNA)
webEmbed.label: Video Activity · Summarise the Role of microRNA (2:28)

keyTakeaways: Embedded YouTube Resource: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cK-OGB1_ELE&t=148s (cued to 2:28 / 148s where microRNA processing and RISC gene silencing are demonstrated).
1. Hairpin Transcription & Export: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are transcribed as primary hairpin precursors (pri-miRNA / pre-miRNA) and exported from the nucleus into the cytoplasm.
2. Cytoplasmic Dicer Cleavage: The cytoplasmic endonuclease Dicer cleaves the hairpin loop to generate a short (~21–22 nucleotide) double-stranded miRNA duplex.
3. RISC Complex Activation: One strand (the guide strand) is loaded into the RNA-Induced Silencing Complex (RISC) containing Argonaute endonuclease, while the passenger strand is degraded.

4. Target mRNA Silencing (AMT-130 Application — P5 & M3): The active miRNA-RISC complex binds via complementary base-pairing to target mRNA (exon 1 of human HTT mRNA in AMT-130), triggering mRNA cleavage/degradation or blocking ribosome translation to reduce toxic mHTT protein synthesis.

reveals.label: Question: Summarise the role of microRNA (miRNA) (P5 & M3)
reveals.question: Watch the video from 2:28 (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cK-OGB1_ELE&t=148s) and summarise the role of microRNA (miRNA) in regulating gene expression.
reveals.answer:
MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are short (~21–22 nucleotide) non-coding RNA molecules that regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally via RNA interference (RNAi):
1. Transcription & Export: Transcribed in the nucleus as stem-loop hairpin precursors (pri-miRNA / pre-miRNA) and exported to the cytoplasm.
2. Dicer Cleavage: The cytoplasmic Dicer enzyme cleaves the hairpin loop into a short double-stranded miRNA duplex.
3. RISC Loading: The single-stranded guide miRNA is incorporated into the RNA-Induced Silencing Complex (RISC), while the passenger strand is discarded.
4. Post-Transcriptional Silencing (AMT-130 Link): The guide miRNA directs RISC to bind complementarily to a target mRNA transcript (such as HTT mRNA in AMT-130), either cleaving/degrading the mRNA or blocking ribosome translation so toxic mutant huntingtin (mHTT) protein cannot be synthesised.

slides.title: Does RNAi Silencing Address Mutant HTT Loss of Function?
slides.subtitle: M4: Analyse the challenges involved with gene therapy for the genetic disorder. (PO3)
keyTakeaways: Criterion M4 (PO3): Analyse the challenges involved with gene therapy for the genetic disorder.
Core Answer — NO: AMT-130 RNAi silencing addresses the toxic gain-of-function of mutant mHTT aggregates, NOT the loss-of-function of wild-type huntingtin (wtHTT).

Wild-Type HTT Essential Physiological Role: Healthy wtHTT is required in neurons for axonal vesicle transport, synaptic survival, anti-apoptotic protection, and stimulating cortical BDNF (Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor) transcription.

Non-Allele-Specific Knockdown Dilemma (M4): Because AMT-130's miHTT targets exon 1 on BOTH mutant mHTT and wild-type wtHTT mRNA transcripts, excessive silencing risks depleting essential wtHTT and worsening loss-of-function pathology.

reveals.label: M4 Challenge Question (PO3): Loss-of-Function Effect of Mutant HTT
reveals.question: M4: Analyse the challenges involved with gene therapy for the genetic disorder. (PO3) — Does RNAi silencing (AMT-130) address the loss-of-function effect of mutant HTT?
reveals.answer: No. Huntington's disease involves both a primary toxic gain-of-function (misfolded polyQ mHTT aggregates) and a loss-of-function of normal wild-type huntingtin (wtHTT), which is essential for axonal transport, synaptic maintenance, and cortical BDNF transcription. Because AMT-130's miHTT is non-allele-specific (binding exon 1 of both mutant and wild-type HTT mRNA), it lowers toxic mHTT but simultaneously reduces healthy wtHTT protein—meaning it does NOT restore loss-of-function and requires careful dose titration to avoid wild-type HTT depletion.

slides.title: Assessment Point 1: HTT Pathology & AMT-130 Mechanism Check
slides.subtitle: Formative Assessment Checkpoint · OCR NEA Task 2 Pass (P5, P7) & Merit (M3, M4)
keyTakeaways: Question 1 (P5 & M3): >36 CAG repeats in HTT exon 1 encode an expanded polyglutamine tract, causing toxic mHTT misfolding and selective GABAergic medium spiny neuron loss in the caudate and putamen; AMT-130 directly targets this root mRNA transcript.
Question 2 (P7 & M4): Recombinant AAV5 capsid delivered via bilateral MRI-guided stereotactic Convection-Enhanced Delivery (CED) directly into the caudate and putamen to bypass the BBB.
Question 3 (P5 & M3): Episomal pri-miHTT is processed by Dicer, loaded into RISC, and base-pairs with HTT mRNA to trigger catalytic mRNA cleavage and reduce toxic mHTT translation.

reveals.label: Question 1: Therapeutic Relevance (P5 & M3)
reveals.question: Explain how an expanded CAG repeat (>36 repeats) in exon 1 of the HTT gene leads to selective death of GABAergic medium spiny neurons, and why AMT-130 is relevant (P5, M3).
reveals.answer: Each CAG codon translates into glutamine (Q). When CAG >36, the elongated polyglutamine tract causes mutant huntingtin (mHTT) protein to misfold and accumulate as toxic intracellular aggregates that selectively trigger apoptosis in GABAergic medium spiny neurons (MSNs) of the caudate nucleus and putamen. AMT-130 is directly relevant (P5, M3) because it silences HTT mRNA upstream of translation.

reveals.label: Question 2: Vector & CED Delivery (P7 & M4)
reveals.question: Explain the method of delivery for AMT-130 and why bilateral MRI-guided Convection-Enhanced Delivery (CED) is required (P7, M4).
reveals.answer: AMT-130 uses a recombinant AAV5 viral capsid administered via a single intracranial stereotactic microinfusion directly into the bilateral caudate nucleus and putamen using real-time MRI-guided Convection-Enhanced Delivery (CED) (P7). While CED bypasses the Blood-Brain Barrier, it presents major surgical and irreversibility challenges (M4).

reveals.label: Question 3: RNAi Silencing Mechanism (P5 & M3)
reveals.question: Trace the intracellular pathway of AMT-130 after AAV5 enters a striatal neuron, explaining how Dicer and RISC lower toxic mHTT protein.
reveals.answer: Once AAV5 forms a nuclear episome, it transcribes pri-miHTT hairpins. In the cytoplasm, the Dicer enzyme cleaves the hairpin into mature miHTT, which loads into the RNA-Induced Silencing Complex (RISC). RISC binds complementarily to HTT mRNA and cleaves it, preventing ribosome translation of toxic mHTT.

slides.title: Learner Activity 1: Auditing NCT04120493 Trial Architecture
slides.subtitle: Paired Critical Thinking Task (8 Minutes) · Criteria M3, M4 (PO3) & D3, D4 (PO4)
keyTakeaways: Task A (Phase I/II Classification): Combined Phase I/II design (N=29: 12 low-dose, 17 high-dose) simultaneously tests neurosurgical safety/tolerability (Phase I) and biological target engagement/proof-of-concept in a rare genetic disorder (Phase II).

Task B (Sham Surgery Justification): Superficial cranial burr-hole drilling without dural penetration ethically blinds patients and clinicians to control for the strong placebo expectation effect of neurosurgery.

Task C (Unblinding Critique — D4): Unblinding sham control patients after 12 months means 24- and 36-month efficacy comparisons must rely on external propensity score-matched natural history cohorts rather than a concurrent blinded placebo arm.

reveals.label: Task A: Phase I/II Classification
reveals.question: Explain why NCT04120493 (29 patients: N=12 low-dose, N=17 high-dose) is a combined Phase I/II trial rather than a pivotal Phase III RCT.
reveals.answer: Because AMT-130 is a first-in-human, irreversible intracranial gene therapy for a rare monogenic disorder, a combined Phase I/II design evaluates acute surgical/dose safety (Phase I) alongside CSF biomarker target engagement and preliminary efficacy (Phase II) before committing hundreds of patients to a Phase III RCT.

reveals.label: Task B: Sham Surgery Justification
reveals.question: Discuss why the control arm underwent imitation surgery (superficial cranial bone drilling without dural penetration) to control for placebo effects.
reveals.answer: Invasive neurosurgery induces a powerful psychological placebo response that can transiently improve subjective motor and functional ratings. Superficial cranial drilling without penetrating the dura mater maintains double-blinding while protecting control patients from intracranial hemorrhage or parenchymal injury.

reveals.label: Task C: Unblinding Critique — D4
reveals.question: Evaluate how unblinding sham control patients after 12 months impacts 36-month comparative data validity (D4).
reveals.answer: Unblinding at 12 months (allowing sham patients to cross over) removes the internal randomized placebo group for years 2 and 3. Consequently, 24- and 36-month efficacy claims must be benchmarked against an external propensity score-matched natural history cohort, which carries higher risk of confounding bias than a blinded RCT arm.

Task C (Unblinding Critique — D4): Unblinding sham control patients after 12 months means 24- and 36-month efficacy comparisons must rely on external propensity score-matched natural history cohorts rather than a concurrent blinded placebo arm.

slides.title: Learner Activity 2: Interpreting CSF Biomarkers & cUHDRS Data
slides.subtitle: Data Analysis Workshop (10 Minutes) · Criteria M4 (PO3) & D3, D4 (PO4)
keyTakeaways: Challenge 1 (The CSF NfL Curve): Acute NfL spike at 1–3 months reflects mechanical axonal trauma from stereotactic microcatheter insertion (M4); the drop to -8.2% below baseline at 36 months indicates long-term slowing of active neurodegeneration (D3, D4).

Challenge 2 (Surrogate vs Functional Endpoints): CSF mHTT lowering proves molecular target engagement (surrogate biomarker), whereas 75% cUHDRS slowing (p=0.003), 59% TMS slowing, and 60% TFC slowing demonstrate real-world preservation of motor, cognitive, and daily living function.

Challenge 3 (Statistical vs Clinical Significance): While p=0.003 shows statistical significance against a matched natural history cohort, small sample size (N=17 high-dose) and non-randomized external comparison require confirmatory Phase III RCT validation.

reveals.label: Challenge 1: The CSF NfL Curve (-8.2% at 36 Months)
reveals.question: Explain why CSF Neurofilament Light (NfL) spikes acutely after surgery before dropping -8.2% below baseline at 36 months.
reveals.answer: Neurofilament Light (NfL) is an intracellular structural protein released into CSF when axons are damaged. Stereotactic catheter insertion causes acute, localized mechanical trauma (initial spike). As surgical inflammation resolves, silences mHTT protects striatal neurons, dropping NfL -8.2% below baseline by 36 months—evidence of reduced ongoing neurodegeneration.

reveals.label: Challenge 2: Surrogate vs Functional Endpoints
reveals.question: Contrast CSF mHTT lowering (target engagement) against functional preservation (75% cUHDRS slowing, p=0.003; 59% TMS slowing; 60% TFC slowing).
reveals.answer: A surrogate biomarker (CSF mHTT reduction) only proves the drug hit its molecular target—it does not guarantee patients feel or function better. Clinical endpoints like cUHDRS (75% slowing), TMS (59% slowing), and TFC (60% slowing) measure tangible preservation of movement, cognition, and independent daily living.

reveals.label: Challenge 3: Statistical vs Clinical Significance
reveals.question: Evaluate why comparing against a propensity score-matched natural history cohort requires Phase III confirmation.
reveals.answer: Although p=0.003 indicates a low probability that the 75% cUHDRS slowing occurred by chance, the high-dose cohort is small (N=17) and compared against an external registry rather than a concurrent blinded placebo group. Unmeasured differences in care or expectation could inflate effect size, requiring a large Phase III RCT.

slides.title: Evaluating Gene Therapy: Challenges & Delivery Risks (M4 — PO3)
slides.subtitle: M4: Analyse the challenges involved with gene therapy for the genetic disorder. (PO3)
keyTakeaways: Surgical Delivery Risks (M4): CED requires invasive open neurosurgery carrying risks of intracranial hemorrhage, infection, and catheter misplacement.
Irreversibility (M4): Permanent genetic alteration with no 'undo button' once AAV5 is infused into the striatum.
Immune & Off-Target Risks (M4): Pre-existing AAV5 neutralizing antibodies, neuroinflammation, and non-allele-specific knockdown of healthy wild-type huntingtin (wtHTT) protein.

slides.title: Assessment Point 2: Evaluating Delivery Risks & Off-Target Effects
slides.subtitle: OCR NEA Task 2 | Criteria M4: Analyse the challenges involved with gene therapy for the genetic disorder (PO3) & D3 (PO4)
keyTakeaways: Risk 1 (Surgical & Irreversibility): Stereotactic CED carries acute hemorrhage/infection risks and permanently transduces neurons with no 'off switch' if chronic toxicity emerges.
Risk 2 (Non-Allele-Specific Knockdown — M4): AMT-130 silences both mutant mHTT and wild-type HTT mRNA; wild-type HTT is essential for vesicular transport, synaptic function, and BDNF neuroprotection.

Risk 3 (Immunological Barriers): Pre-existing anti-AAV5 neutralizing antibodies or capsid-triggered T-cell neuroinflammation can neutralize vectors or damage transduced striatal tissue, preventing repeat dosing.

reveals.label: Risk 1: Surgical & Irreversibility Challenges (M4)
reveals.question: Analyse the surgical risks of stereotactic CED and the clinical implications of administering a permanent AAV5 vector with no 'undo button' (M4).
reveals.answer: Intracranial catheter placement risks hemorrhage, stroke, oedema, and infection. Furthermore, because AAV5 episomes continuously express miHTT for years with no molecular 'off switch', any late-onset neurotoxicity or off-target gene silencing cannot be reversed or washed out.

reveals.label: Risk 2: Non-Allele-Specific Knockdown (M4 & D3)
reveals.question: Why is lowering both toxic mutant huntingtin (mHTT) and healthy wild-type huntingtin (wtHTT) a biological risk for long-term neuronal survival?
reveals.answer: Wild-type huntingtin (wtHTT) plays vital physiological roles in adult neurons, including axonal vesicular transport, anti-apoptotic protection, and promoting Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) transcription. Excessive knockdown of wtHTT alongside mHTT could impair normal neuronal survival.

reveals.label: Risk 3: Immunological Barriers (M4)
reveals.question: Explain why pre-existing AAV5 neutralizing antibodies and potential neuroinflammation must be screened and managed.
reveals.answer: Patients with high pre-existing anti-AAV5 neutralizing antibodies may clear the vector before transduction. Additionally, high viral capsid doses in the CNS can provoke innate microglial activation or cytotoxic T-cell neuroinflammation, requiring perioperative immunosuppression and precluding re-administration.

slides.title: Learner Activity 3: Genetic Counselling & Bioethics Case Study
slides.subtitle: Clinical Consultation Roleplay (10 Minutes) · Criteria P8 (PO2) & M5 (PO3)
keyTakeaways: Patient Scenario (Maya, Age 26): Father diagnosed with 44 CAG repeats (full penetrance); Maya faces a 50% autosomal dominant inheritance risk.
Consultation Task 1 (Autonomy & Testing — P8): Explain 50% risk, 100% penetrance if ≥40 repeats, respect 'The Right Not to Know', and outline PGD/IVF reproductive options.
Consultation Task 2 (Managing Expectations — M5): Clarify that AMT-130 is disease-slowing (not regenerative for lost striatal neurons) and explain informed consent for double-blind sham surgery.

reveals.label: Consultation Task 1: Autonomy & Testing — P8
reveals.question: Advise Maya on her 50% autosomal dominant risk, 100% penetrance, pre-implantation genetic diagnosis (PGD/IVF), and 'The Right Not to Know' (P8).
reveals.answer: Maya has a 50% chance of having inherited the expanded allele from her father. Because 44 CAG repeats exceeds the ≥40 threshold, inheriting it carries 100% lifetime penetrance. The counsellor must protect her autonomy ('The Right Not to Know' if she prefers not to take a presymptomatic test now) and explain that IVF with Pre-Implantation Genetic Diagnosis (PGD) can select unaffected embryos.

reveals.label: Consultation Task 2: Managing Expectations — M5
reveals.question: Explain clearly why AMT-130 slows progression rather than regenerating lost striatal neurons, and explain sham surgery trial consent (M5).
reveals.answer: AMT-130 lowers mHTT protein to protect surviving medium spiny neurons and slow further decline (75% cUHDRS slowing), but it cannot regenerate neurons that have already undergone apoptosis. For clinical trial consent, Maya's father must understand the 12-month randomized double-blind sham surgery arm (superficial burr holes without dural entry) and the permanent nature of AAV5 infusion.

slides.subtitle: Final Synthesis & Self-Assessment · OCR NEA Task 2 Distinction (D3, D4 & D5)
keyTakeaways: Card 1 (Evaluating Functional Cure Viability — D3): AMT-130 shows strong disease-modifying deceleration (75% cUHDRS slowing, -8.2% CSF NfL) but slows progression rather than regenerating lost neurons.

Card 2 (Methodological & Risk Critique — M4, D4 & D5): Weigh small sample size (N=29), 12-month sham unblinding, invasive CED surgery, and non-allele-specific wtHTT knockdown against the lack of curative alternatives.

reveals.label: Synthesis 1: Evaluating Functional Cure Viability (D3)
reveals.question: Draft a 3-sentence Distinction conclusion evaluating whether AMT-130 represents a viable path to a functional cure for Huntington's disease (D3).
reveals.answer: AMT-130 provides compelling Phase I/II proof-of-concept as a disease-modifying therapy, achieving sustained CSF mHTT knockdown, an 8.2% reduction in CSF NfL below baseline, and a 75% slowing of cUHDRS clinical decline at 36 months. However, because AAV5-miHTT silences mRNA without regenerating already-lost striatal medium spiny neurons, it functions as a disease-stabilizing intervention rather than a restorative cure. Therefore, its greatest viability as a functional cure depends on early presymptomatic or prodromal administration before irreversible striatal atrophy occurs.

reveals.label: Synthesis 2: Methodological & Risk Critique (M4, D4 & D5)
reveals.question: Weigh the methodological limitations (N=29 sample size, 12-month sham unblinding) and biological risks (non-allele-specific wtHTT knockdown, irreversible CED neurosurgery) against the urgent clinical need in HD.
reveals.answer: While the small cohort (N=29) and reliance on external natural history controls after 12-month sham unblinding limit statistical certainty, and bilateral CED neurosurgery carries irreversible risks of wtHTT depletion and surgical trauma (M4), Huntington's disease is uniformly fatal with no approved disease-modifying treatments. Consequently, the favourable 36-month risk-benefit profile justifies advancing AMT-130 into pivotal Phase III trials with rigorous long-term safety monitoring (D4, D5).

reveals.label: Synthesis 3: Task 2 Self-Audit Checklist (P5–P8, M3–M5, D3–D5)
reveals.question: How do you verify your NEA Task 2 submission meets every Pass, Merit, and Distinction criterion?
reveals.answer:
1. Pass (PO2): Describe HTT CAG expansion & relevance of AMT-130 (P5), explain AAV5 & MRI-guided stereotactic CED delivery (P7), and summarise genetic counselling for predictive testing & PGD (P8).
2. Merit (PO3): Deepen how Dicer/RISC RNAi silences HTT mRNA (M3), analyse surgical, immune, and non-allele-specific wtHTT loss-of-function challenges (M4), and explain psychological/consent benefits of counselling (M5).
3. Distinction (PO4): Critically evaluate whether AMT-130 is a viable functional cure (D3) and evaluate trial methodology, CSF mHTT/NfL vs cUHDRS endpoints, and holistic patient care (D4, D5).
